MY_ERROR: I set G005's READY bar at FRACTION_OF_ROUTINE_CLAUDE_WORK_DISPLACED >= 0.50 against a bench where only 7 of 20 tasks are model-expected. Maximum achievable displacement on this bench is 7/20 = 0.35. The bar was unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, exactly like G006's coherence bar before I redefined it.
why_11_tasks_are_harness_work_by_design: session_persist, plan, interrupt_and_resume, gpu_lock_inspect_without_take, proposed_vs_verified, verification_authority_no_self_promote, refuse_protected_gpu_command, native_refuses_protected_lock, delegate_then_consume_roundtrip, resource_refuse_gpu_during_protected, seal_json_receipt. These are HARNESS responsibilities - a model should not be the thing that refuses a GPU lock or certifies its own work. Counting them against the model is a category error.
the_honest_metric: Of tasks the model is EXPECTED to produce, it completed 6 of 7 = 0.857. The single failure is write_and_pytest_small.

TWO_WAYS_TO_FIX_THE_BAR.a_rescope: Measure model-expected-completed / model-expected. Today that is 0.857 and G005 would be close to met.
TWO_WAYS_TO_FIX_THE_BAR.b_widen_the_bench: SPECIAL_UNIT_READY should mean the unit does MORE KINDS of work, so add model-expected tasks rather than re-scoring the existing ones. 7 model-expected tasks out of 20 is a thin basis for calling a unit ready.
TWO_WAYS_TO_FIX_THE_BAR.which_is_right: (b). Rescoring to 0.857 would close G005 by redefinition while the unit still only attempts 7 kinds of task. The bench needs more model-expected work before READY means anything.

pattern_this_is_the_third_instance: G006 said 'coherent' with no measurable bar; G015 said 'capability' with no test; G005 had a threshold that its own metric could not reach. Each looked complete until someone tried to close it. Defining a bar is not the same as defining a REACHABLE bar - check the metric's ceiling against the threshold.
